bibliography.title: Hydrogen ion conducting starch-chitosan blend based electrolyte for application in electrochemical devices
bibliography.authors: a  Institute of Graduate Studies, University of Malaya, 50603 Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia b  Centre for Foundation Studies in Science, University of Malaya, 50603 Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

system_identity.base_material: Starch–chitosan blend polymer electrolyte (80 wt.% starch / 20 wt.% chitosan).
system_identity.dopant: NH4Cl (proton donor) and glycerol plasticizer (highest conductivity reported at 35 wt.% glycerol in prior work referenced as P7).
system_identity.other: Starch dissolved in 1% acetic acid; chitosan >75% deacetylated; corn starch used.

measurement_scope.other_conditions: Electrolytes prepared by solution casting; materials processing included 80°C dissolution for starch in 1% acetic acid for 20 min (Experimental 2.1, truncated).

mechanism_relevant_findings: Transference number measurements indicate ions are the dominant conducting species in the electrolyte (Abstract).
The cation transference number for the highest-conducting electrolyte is reported as t+ = 0.56 (Abstract).
NH4Cl is described as a proton donor for polymer electrolytes in this system (Introduction).

numerical_findings.metric: Room-temperature ionic conductivity (highest conducting electrolyte, from authors' previous work cited)
numerical_findings.conditions: Starch–chitosan–NH4Cl plasticized with 35 wt.% glycerol (P7 electrolyte); referenced in Introduction citing previous work [19].

numerical_findings.metric: Primary proton battery open-circuit potential stability duration

limitations: No impedance spectroscopy frequency range, temperature range, or Nyquist/Bode features are provided in the supplied truncated text.

Humidity/water-activity control conditions are not stated in the supplied truncated text.

relevance_judgement.reason: The excerpt identifies a proton-donor salt system and provides ion/cation transference information and conductivity magnitude but lacks EIS/Arrhenius/VTF details needed for mechanism discrimination.
